decision: Plan CR-A as one method change, `config-include-overrides`, with deltas to four existing specs (config-loading, config-set, config-show, config-sync) and no new capability
Mark the change to where new keys are written (into overrides, not the included file) as BREAKING
reason: Before this change, set wrote new keys under an include into the included file itself

decision: With nested includes, a new key goes into the nearest file that holds the include reference (e.g. agents/coder.yaml), not always into troupe.yml
reason: The contract defines the including file as 'the file that contains the include reference'; confirmed by the product owner

decision: An include with overrides whose content is a list, a scalar or an empty file fails to load with exit 4
reason: Deep-merge is only defined between mappings; any guess could show a value nobody wrote; refusing loses nothing and can be relaxed later; an empty file loads as null

decision: A `$ref` whose value is not an include string (e.g. `$ref: hello`) stays an ordinary key
reason: Every file that loads today keeps loading the same; exit 4 would break files for a case the contract does not mention

decision: Deleting a key that both the included file and an override set removes it from both files
reason: Overrides cannot delete, so removing only the override would bring the included value back and the verifier would refuse with exit 3

decision: An override mapping left empty by a delete is removed, but the `$ref` mapping stays in mapping form and is not converted back to scalar form
reason: An empty override changes nothing and would be clutter; keeping mapping form means the delete changes only the lines it must
recorded_at: design.md D9 and Non-Goals (diff.patch:200,312-315); questions.md:51; README decision 30

decision: A list item that is an include converts to the compact form `- $ref: STRING`, with the overrides at the string's column
options: a bare `-` with an indented mapping below
reason: The smallest edit; keeps the item's comment on its line; it is how `show` prints list items that are mappings

decision: `set coder file:…` on a mapping-form include that has overrides is refused with exit 3 (the bare include string is 'unchanged' only when there are no overrides)
reason: It replaces a value whose whole value comes from an include, so overrides are never dropped silently (covered by the contract)

decision: Converting a block mapping entry removes the string and the whitespace before it, keeps the rest of the line (`coder:  # c`), and indents `$ref` one indentation unit of the including file deeper
options: keep rest of line as in the contract example
the column-keeping rule of 'Scalar replaced by a block collection'
reason: Matches the contract's example

decision: A whole-document include converts by inserting `$ref: ` with entries at column 0; a flow include converts to `{$ref: STRING, k: v}`
The converted `$ref` value keeps the include string's original bytes and quotes; new overrides copy the quoting of the preceding entry
Converting a block-scalar include string to mapping form is refused with WriteRefused (exit 3)
Drop the `string.tagged` check from the conversion guard
reason: A tagged string can never be an include (include_target already excludes it)

decision: Put the `$ref` syntax and merge rule in a new module `overrides.py`, not in loader.py
reason: The write side needs the same rules, and loader.py is about files and includes

decision: Merged mappings keep `layers` (the physical mappings they were built from) and Include gets `overrides`, so the tree stays physical nodes wherever values are written
options: keep the physical tree and compute merged data separately
reason: Otherwise get/show/--sources/reconcile/verify would all need a second path

decision: Move `include_target`/`INCLUDE_PREFIX` from loader.py to tree.py
When an override value is itself an include that merges with base content, the merged node takes the override's include (the nearest one wins)
reason: It is the nearest include

decision: One function, `plan.new_key_target`, decides where a new key goes and returns a new `AddOverride` op; descending into a list item clears the anchor
reason: Overrides cannot address list items

decision: Existing values are replaced in the last layer that sets them; a merged mapping replaced by a non-mapping is replaced in its outermost override layer
reason: Its winning entry is the override's

decision: Keep the read-back verifier as the safety net, so wrong placements are refused with exit 3 (including setting a key named `$ref`)
reason: Better to refuse than to write wrongly

decision: Make no code changes for reconcile, history or watch; prove their behaviour with tests instead
reason: They already see merged data and config.files, which includes files reached through $ref

decision: Non-goals: no tombstone deletes, no list merging or addressing list items through overrides, no conversion back to scalar form, no replacing a whole include
Accept that an existing mapping holding `$ref: file:…` as plain data now loads as an include, and note it in the README
reason: Unlikely in troupe configurations; the data stays in the files unchanged

decision: Document in the README that mapping-form includes need step 5 or later, and that rolling back means rewriting them by hand
reason: Step-4 code reads `$ref` as an ordinary key

decision: Keep the existing scenario name 'New key inside an included mapping' rather than renaming it
options: keep the name and change only its content
reason: The validator wants the existing scenario name kept

decision: Fix an existing bug: `owned_end` of an included value ends at its reference in the including file
reason: The insertion point was measured in the included file, so set failed with exit 3; overrides depend on the same code

decision: Replace the old test 'new key inside an included mapping goes into that file' with its opposite
reason: The spec scenario now expects an override

decision: Correct task 4.1: a new override's history event has old null, not 0.2
reason: The key did not exist before; an existing 0.2 would be changed in the included file instead

decision: Fix the smoke test's expected output to show the CRLF prompt double-quoted instead of as a literal block
reason: A string containing CR can't go in a literal block, so show double-quotes it, as the spec requires

decision: Restructure `_apply` so one op can produce edits for several files, grouped by file
reason: A delete across layers needs it

decision: Run the formatter, then shorten the lines that are genuinely too long
reason: Linter and formatter use the same limit; the formatter was right that the signature fits

decision: Amend the unpushed group-2 commit to fold in the formatter fix
reason: It was committed before the formatter ran and had not been pushed

decision: Verify key tests by deliberately breaking the code (mutation checks)
reason: Tasks require showing the tests catch breakage

decision: Reference the design at its current path in the README and update the link when archiving
reason: Archiving moves the file under archive/

decision: Sync CR-A's spec deltas into spec/spec before archiving, instead of archiving without syncing
reason: Without the sync the main specs would contradict code and tests; syncing touches only spec files and matches earlier archives; the fallback reply asked for the safest assumption

decision: When syncing, modified requirements replace their block in place and added requirements go at the end; then check that nothing was lost
Plan CR-B as a separate change `config-set-in-include` built on CR-A, with CR-A applied and archived first
reason: CR-B depends on CR-A's new_key_target

decision: Implement CR-A before CR-B even though CR-B arrived and was planned in the middle
`--in-include` is a store_true flag that can go anywhere after `set`, like `--reason`
`--in-include` affects only new keys; existing values, appends and deletes follow CR-A
reason: Otherwise the flag could write a value that an override then hides

decision: With no include involved, `--in-include` is accepted and changes nothing
reason: The step-1 rule picks the same file; refusing would force scripts to check for includes first

decision: With `--in-include`, a merged ancestor's key goes into the included content's file, and an override-only ancestor's key goes into the override's file
reason: That is where the shared content lives; an override-only section has no included file, and the step-1 rule names the override's file

decision: With `--in-include` and nested includes, the key goes into the innermost included file
reason: That is the file that holds the deepest existing ancestor

decision: `--in-include` adds no exit codes and does not change history; the flag is not recorded in history
reason: It changes placement, not meaning; history records values, not files
recorded_at: design.md D3 and Non-Goals (diff.patch:874,909-910); README decision 38

decision: Pass the flag as a keyword argument down to `new_key_target`, which returns a plain AddKey
options: a post-pass that rewrites AddOverride into AddKey
reason: Otherwise two places would know the rule

decision: Resolve AddKey parents through `physical_mapping` = layers[0] (the innermost), with merge flattening layers
reason: layers[0] is always the innermost included file's mapping

decision: CR-B non-goals: not the default, no per-theatre setting, no moving existing overrides
Add a nested case with a `$ref` mapping in the middle file, which the spec does not have
reason: The spec's nested example can't tell innermost from outermost

decision: Check CR-B task 1.1 from the archived tasks, the archive commit and the passing suite instead of `method status`
reason: The archived change is no longer found by its status command

decision: Sync CR-B's spec deltas before archiving, as for CR-A
reason: Following the earlier 'safest option' instruction; otherwise the specs would lack --in-include

decision: Record each out-of-contract choice, with its reason, in the README decisions list (26–38)
